inference_timing.note: In latent space, DDPM (1000 steps) and DDIM (50 steps) take roughly the same wall-clock time per batch, unlike pixel space where DDIM is dramatically faster. Each latent-space denoising step is cheap relative to the fixed per-call overhead, so reducing step count from 1000 to 50 does not yield the ~20x speedup seen in pixel-space DDPM.

notes: FID/IS evaluation took ~9 minutes in latent space, versus ~2 hours for the equivalent pixel-space DDPM evaluation (see experiments/pixel_ddpm/cosine_ema_logit_v2_100/evaluation/results.json), because each denoising step operates on an 8x8 latent grid rather than a 64x64 pixel grid. This is documented as a training/inference cost observation, not a quality claim - see README.md's Latent DDPM section for the corresponding quality discussion (blurrier outputs than pixel-space DDPM, likely bottlenecked by the VAE's reconstruction quality).
